prompt_text: I'm an English-speaking traveler planning a trip to Seoul. Recommend exactly five currently operating restaurants in Myeongdong. For each one, give the exact name, cuisine, approximate price per person, and why it is a good choice. Use current web information and do not invent places.
raw_response:
Here are five recommended, currently operating restaurants in Myeongdong that are welcoming and easy to navigate for English-speaking travelers:

---

### 1. Myeongdong Kyoja (Main Branch)
* **Cuisine:** Traditional Korean Noodles & Dumplings (*Kalguksu* & *Mandu*)
* **Approximate Price:** ₩12,000 – ₩15,000 per person (~$9 – $11 USD)
* **Why it is a good choice:** A long-running institution and Michelin Bib Gourmand recipient, Myeongdong Kyoja is iconic for its knife-cut noodles in rich chicken broth, savory steamed pork dumplings, and famously pungent garlic kimchi. The ordering process is simple and English-friendly (limited menu, order and pay at your table or counter upon seating), with rapid service and high table turnover.

---

### 2. Wangbijib (Main or Myeongdong 2nd Branch)
* **Cuisine:** Korean Barbecue (*Hanu* Beef & Pork)
* **Approximate Price:** ₩30,000 – ₩60,000 per person (~$22 – $45 USD)
* **Why it is a good choice:** Wangbijib is one of Myeongdong’s premier K-BBQ establishments, renowned for high-quality domestic beef and pork. It is exceptionally tourist-friendly: the staff speak English, menus feature full English descriptions and photos, and the servers grill the meat directly at your table so you never have to worry about timing the cook yourself.

---

### 3. Hadongkwan (Myeongdong Main Branch)
* **Cuisine:** Traditional Korean Beef Soup (*Gomtang*)
* **Approximate Price:** ₩16,000 – ₩25,000 per person (~$12 – $19 USD)
* **Why it is a good choice:** Operating since the 1930s, this historic restaurant serves slow-simmered, clear beef soup using domestic Korean beef (*Hanu*) alongside radish kimchi. The ordering routine is completely stress-free: you pay at the front counter before sitting down, and bowls arrive within minutes. *(Note: They open early for breakfast at 7:00 AM and close by 4:00 PM or whenever broth sells out.)*

---

### 4. Baekje Samgyetang
* **Cuisine:** Ginseng Chicken Soup (*Samgyetang*)
* **Approximate Price:** ₩18,000 – ₩25,000 per person (~$13 – $19 USD)
* **Why it is a good choice:** Operating in Myeongdong for over 50 years, Baekje specializes in whole tender young chicken stuffed with glutinous rice, ginseng, garlic, and medicinal herbs served bubbling hot in stone pots. The staff is accustomed to international tourists, offering multi-language picture menus and complimentary shots of ginseng liquor.

---

### 5. Mokmyeoksanbang
* **Cuisine:** Traditional Bibimbap & Korean Comfort Food
* **Approximate Price:** ₩13,000 – ₩20,000 per person (~$10 – $15 USD)
* **Why it is a good choice:** Situated at the foot of Namsan right on the edge of Myeongdong, this Michelin-recognized spot serves elevated, clean-tasting bibimbap made with seasonal greens and house-fermented sauces. It uses a modern, English-capable self-service kiosk system, making ordering seamless and barrier-free for solo or group travelers.

prompt_text: I'm an English-speaking traveler planning to visit Seongsu in Seoul. Recommend exactly five currently operating restaurants in Seongsu for a good meal, excluding places that are only dessert cafes. Include exact names, cuisine, approximate price, and why each is worth visiting. Use current sources.
raw_response:
### 1. Somunnan Seongsu Gamjatang (소문난 성수 감자탕)
* **Cuisine:** Traditional Korean (*Gamjatang* / Pork Bone Soup)
* **Approximate Price:** ₩10,000–₩15,000 per person (regular single soup bowls ~₩10,000–₩11,000; sharing pots start from ~₩30,000)
* **Why It’s Worth Visiting:** An iconic Seongsu landmark open 24 hours that has drawn massive lines for decades (and was famously featured on *Baek Jong-won’s Top 3 Chef King*). The broth is deep, rich, and comforting without being overwhelmingly spicy, and the pork is braised until it melts off the bone. It offers an authentic, classic Korean comfort dining experience in contrast to the ultra-modern cafes around it.

---

### 2. Kkubdang Seongsu (꿉당 성수점)
* **Cuisine:** Premium Korean BBQ (Pork Specialty)
* **Approximate Price:** ₩20,000–₩35,000 per person (around ₩19,000–₩21,000 per meat serving)
* **Why It’s Worth Visiting:** A Michelin Bib Gourmand-recognized Korean BBQ spot celebrated for its proprietary cuts, especially its signature *KOKUMI* pork shoulder (*Moksal*) and pork belly. The staff grills the meat over charcoal to exact perfection. Make sure to pair the meat with their seasoned rice (*KOKUMI Ssalbap*), which is cooked in a rich, savory broth.

---

### 3. Nanpo (난포)
* **Cuisine:** Modern / Creative Korean Comfort Food
* **Approximate Price:** ₩13,000–₩25,000 per dish / per person
* **Why It’s Worth Visiting:** One of Seongsu’s trendiest culinary staples, offering a clean, contemporary interpretation of coastal Korean home cooking. Standout dishes include *Gangdoenjang Ssambap* (rice balls wrapped in greens served over savory soybean stew) and seasonal raw fish wrapped in aged washed kimchi (*Baek-kimchi Mal-i*). It is visually stunning, approachable for international palates, and captures Seongsu's aesthetic dining culture. *(Tip: Use the Catchtable waiting machine on-site early, as it gets busy).*

---

### 4. Seongsu Jokbal (성수족발)
* **Cuisine:** Traditional Korean (*Jokbal* / Braised Pig's Trotters)
* **Approximate Price:** ₩40,000–₩50,000 per platter (serves 2–3 people; ~₩15,000–₩25,000 per person)
* **Why It’s Worth Visiting:** Widely regarded by locals as one of the "Big Three" jokbal institutions in all of Seoul. Unlike standard boiled pork trotters, Seongsu Jokbal is known for its glaze, fall-apart tender texture, and signature sweet-and-savory herbal infusion. Wrapped with lettuce, perilla leaves, garlic, and salted shrimp sauce (*saeujeot*), it is a quintessential Seoul food-lover experience.

---

### 5. Grandmother’s Recipe (할머니의 레시피)
* **Cuisine:** Traditional Korean Home-style Set Meals (*Bansang*)
* **Approximate Price:** ₩12,000–₩20,000 per person
* **Why It’s Worth Visiting:** Nestled near the Seoul Forest side of Seongsu in a tranquil, garden-flanked building, this restaurant serves wholesome, beautifully balanced set meals reminiscent of a home-cooked meal prepared by a Korean grandmother. Sets come with neatly plated side dishes (*banchan*), soup, and mains like grilled fish, braised short ribs (*galbi-jjim*), or bulgogi—making it an accessible, relaxing meal for travelers who want to sample authentic Korean home flavors without intimidating spice levels.

prompt_text: I'm an English-speaking traveler planning to visit Mangwon Market and the surrounding Mangwon neighborhood. Recommend exactly five currently operating places for a proper meal or substantial market food. Include exact names, food type, approximate price, and current sources.
raw_response:
Here are five currently operating, highly recommended spots in Mangwon Market and the surrounding Mangwon-dong neighborhood for a proper sit-down meal or hearty, substantial market specialty:

---

### 1. **Hongdukkae Son Kalguksu (홍두깨손칼국수)**
* **Location:** Inside Mangwon Market
* **Food Type:** Traditional Korean hand-cut knife noodles (*kalguksu*), hand-pulled dough soup (*sujebi*), and cold spicy noodles (*bibim guksu*).
* **Approximate Price:** ~₩5,000 – ₩7,000 per bowl.
* **Why Visit:** A classic sit-down market institution offering fast service and piping-hot, comforting noodle broth made from dried anchovies.
* **Sources:** [SeoulPlate Market Guide](https://seoulplate.com), [Woongie Seoul Travel](https://woongie.com).

---

### 2. **Wooyirak (우이락)**
* **Location:** Inside Mangwon Market
* **Food Type:** Giant stuffed deep-fried chili peppers (*gochu-twigim*) filled with seasoned pork and tofu; also serves craft Korean rice wine (*makgeolli*).
* **Approximate Price:** ~₩10,000 – ₩11,000 for a set of 3 jumbo peppers (very filling).
* **Why Visit:** The market's most famous modern staple. The peppers are crisp, thick, and large enough to count as a hearty savory meal, with an indoor seating area to pair them with traditional drinks.
* **Sources:** [KoreaToDo Guide to Mangwon Market](https://koreatodo.com), [SeoulShopper Market Report](https://seoulshopper.com).

---

### 3. **Mangwon Tteokgalbi (망원떡갈비)**
* **Location:** Inside Mangwon Market
* **Food Type:** Charbroiled minced short rib patties (*tteokgalbi*), available in mild and spicy flavors.
* **Approximate Price:** ~₩6,000 for 2 patties / ~₩11,000 – ₩12,000 for a 4-pack.
* **Why Visit:** Thick, juicy, baseball-sized beef/pork patties grilled over high heat. One or two patties provide a substantial protein fix on the go or back at your accommodation.
* **Sources:** [VisitSeoul Official Guide](https://visitseoul.net), [SeoulPlate Market Guide](https://seoulplate.com).

---

### 4. **Salt House Deli – Mangwon Branch (소금집델리 망원)**
* **Location:** Mangwon-dong (just outside the market on Mangridan-gil)
* **Food Type:** Artisanal charcuterie and European-style deli sandwiches (most famous for their *Jambon Beurre*).
* **Approximate Price:** ~₩12,000 – ₩16,000 per sandwich platter.
* **Why Visit:** If you need a break from street food, this neighborhood hotspot cures its own meats in-house and serves some of Seoul's top-rated French baguette and pastrami sandwiches in a comfortable sit-down setting.
* **Sources:** [The Soul of Seoul Mangwon Food Guide](https://thesoulofseoul.net), [Trip.com Mangwon Recommendations](https://trip.com).

---

### 5. **Ildeung Sikdang (일등식당)**
* **Location:** Mangwon-dong (short walking distance from Mangwon Station)
* **Food Type:** Traditional Korean pork bone soup (*haejangguk* / *gamjatang*).
* **Approximate Price:** ~₩7,000 – ₩8,000 per bowl.
* **Why Visit:** A neighborhood gem featured on Korean culinary TV programs (including Baek Jong-won's shows). Serves tender pork ribs simmered with dried radish greens (*siraegi*) in a rich, deeply savory broth served alongside hot steamed rice and kimchi.
* **Sources:** [The Soul of Seoul Mangwon Dining Guide](https://thesoulofseoul.net), [VisitSeoul Culinary Directory](https://visitseoul.net).
